title.es: Verbos de información y sus estructuras

summary.en: Instead of always using _say_ and _tell_, skilled speakers choose a verb that shows the speaker's purpose: _admit_, _deny_, _warn_, _urge_, _accuse_. Each verb has its own pattern. Some take a **that-clause** (_He claimed that…_), some a **to-infinitive** (_She refused to…_), some an **-ing form** (_He denied taking…_), and many take **object + to-infinitive** (_They urged us to…_). Verbs of blame and criticism take **object + preposition + -ing** (_accuse someone of lying_). Using the exact verb makes a report shorter and more precise, which helps in Speaking part 4 and in the formal email of Writing part 4.
summary.es: En español basta con «dijo que…»; en inglés, el verbo ya lleva la intención (acusó, admitió, advirtió) y cada uno tiene su estructura. Acusar de hacer algo es **accuse + objeto + of + -ing**.

form: **+ that-clause**: _claim, explain, insist, point out, mention, admit, complain_ (_He insisted that he was right._)
**+ to-infinitive**: _agree, offer, promise, refuse, threaten, claim_ (_She refused to sign._)
**+ -ing**: _admit, deny, suggest, recommend, mention_ (_He admitted taking the money._)
**+ object + to-infinitive**: _advise, ask, encourage, invite, order, persuade, remind, urge, warn_ (_They warned us not to go._)
**+ object + preposition + -ing**: _accuse … of, blame … for, criticise … for, congratulate … on, thank … for_
**apologise (to someone) for + -ing**; **insist on + -ing**; **blame something on someone**

uses.text: **Showing attitude** → _She accused the company of ignoring complaints._
**Admitting or denying** → _The driver admitted driving too fast. He denied causing the accident._
**Advising and warning** → _The guide urged everyone to stay together._
**Promises and refusals** → _The shop promised to refund the money, but refused to replace the item._
**Reporting a complaint formally** → _I would like to point out that the room was not cleaned._

note.en: Verbs such as point out, complain and regret to inform sound polite and precise in a formal email.
note.es: Verbos como point out o complain son corteses y precisos en un correo formal.

mistakes.wrong: He accused me to have lied.

why.en: Accuse takes object + of + -ing form, not a to-infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: She insisted to pay for the meal.
mistakes.right: She insisted on paying for the meal.

why.en: Insist is followed by on + -ing, or by a that-clause.

mistakes.wrong: They blamed the delay to the weather.
mistakes.right: They blamed the delay on the weather.

why.en: Blame something on a cause, or blame someone for something.
why.es: Blame something on…; blame someone for…

mistakes.wrong: He denied to have taken the keys.

why.en: Deny is followed by an -ing form (or having + past participle), not to-infinitive.

examples.en: The manager accused her of falsifying the figures.
examples.es: El director la acusó de falsificar las cifras.

examples.en: He refused to answer any questions about the contract.
She finally admitted sending the email by mistake.
The tutor urged us to submit the draft early.
examples.es: El tutor nos instó a entregar el borrador pronto.

examples.en: The passengers complained that nobody had explained the delay.
He denied having seen the report before the meeting.
The doctor warned him not to lift heavy objects.
My neighbour apologised for making so much noise.
They criticised the council for ignoring the problem.
The union insisted on being present at the talks.
She reminded us to bring our passports to the airport.

practice.prompt: The manager accused her ___ the figures.
He refused ___ any questions about the contract.

explanation.en: Refuse is followed by a to-infinitive.

practice.prompt: She finally admitted ___ the email by mistake.

explanation.en: Admit is followed by an -ing form (or a that-clause with a proper verb form).

practice.prompt: The tutor ___ us to submit the draft early.

explanation.en: Urge takes object + to-infinitive; suggest and insist do not.
